cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, who he calls his child. He just told Timothy that everyone in the province of Asia deserted him (2 Timothy 1:15). And now Paul tells him one thing first: be STRONG.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to be strong. Strong in what?

answers.text: The grace that is in Christ Jesus
His own hard training and effort
The wisdom of the older leaders

cards.text: Everything Timothy heard Paul say in front of many witnesses, he's supposed to entrust to faithful men. Not lock it away in a drawer, friend, because I can tell you from EXPERIENCE: nothing gets passed on from the back of a drawer.

cards.question: Timothy is to entrust Paul's teaching to faithful men. What should those men be qualified to do?

cards.text: Then Paul paints a picture. Timothy's a soldier, a good soldier of Christ Jesus, and Paul wants him to join in something right alongside him.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to join him in ___ like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

cards.text: A soldier doesn't get tangled up in civilian affairs. You will NEVER see a soldier in the middle of a mission go, "Hold on, hold on, HOLD ON, I gotta answer the group chat."

cards.question: A soldier stays out of civilian affairs. Why does he do it?

answers.text: To please the one who enlisted him
To earn a higher rank someday
To keep himself out of danger

cards.text: Second picture: an athlete in a competition, going for the crown. Me? I race my oven timer every morning on a gold base, and friend, that timer is UNDEFEATED.

cards.question: A competitor doesn't receive the crown unless he competes according to the ___.

cards.text: Third picture: a farmer. He works hard in his field, and then the crops come in.

cards.question: Paul says the hardworking farmer should be the last to partake of the crops.
Soldier, athlete, farmer. Paul tells Timothy to consider what he's saying. Who will give Timothy insight into all things?

cards.text: Now Paul gets to the heart of it. He tells Timothy to remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, just as Paul's gospel proclaims.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead and descended from ___.

cards.text: That gospel is why Paul is suffering. He's chained like a criminal, friend, and here I was for YEARS complaining about a drawer.

cards.question: Paul is chained like a criminal for the gospel. What does he say cannot be chained?
Paul says he endures all things for the sake of the elect. Why?

answers.text: So they too may obtain salvation
So he can be set free soon
So the church will honor him

cards.text: Then Paul shares a trustworthy saying: if we died with Him, we'll also live with Him, and if we endure, we'll also reign with Him. Friend, that's the kind of promise you tape right to the oven door.

cards.question: The trustworthy saying goes on: if we deny Him, He will also deny us.

cards.text: And then the saying's last line: if we are faithless, He remains faithful. I know a little something about being found after you've given up on yourself.

cards.question: The saying says that if we are faithless, He remains faithful. Why?

findings.problem: The card states a fact from outside the passage, "Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus" (2 Timothy 1:1), with no reference. The 1:15 fact on the same card has its reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The drawer joke ("Not lock it away in a drawer... nothing gets passed on from the back of a drawer") hints at passing the teaching on. It also rules out the wrong answer "Guard it in silence" on card 4.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "Timeothy's a soldier" drops the comparison. 2 Timothy 2:3 says "like a good soldier of Christ Jesus," so the "like" has to stay.

In the joke "I race my oven timer every morning on a gold base," the "on a gold base" part reads as confusing. The joke also leaves out the point of 2:5, which is competing by the rules. A stranger would likely say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The right answer "The Lord" is much shorter than the wrong answers "His mother Eunice" and "Paul's friend Onesiphorus," so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: "Here I was for YEARS complaining about a drawer" adds something new to his backstory. The backstory says that in the drawer he "didn't talk much" and later spent his time welcoming newcomers. It never says he complained for years.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Story card 6 presents the saying only as promises ("the kind of promise you tape right to the oven door"), and nothing sets up the turn to a warning. The baker can't reason out whether "if we deny Him, He will also deny us" is true, so the card only tests whether they can guess the next line. It should set up the turn in the saying and ask about that change.

rule.text: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
